claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling constitutes a developmental pathway crucial for embryonic tissue morphogenesis, reproduction and adult tissue regeneration.
source: Wnt5a-Ror signaling constitutes a developmental pathway crucial for embryonic tissue morphogenesis, reproduction and adult tissue regeneration, yet the molecular mechanisms by which the Wnt5a-Ror pathway mediates these processes are largely unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about the Wnt5a-Ror pathway, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The molecular mechanisms by which the Wnt5a-Ror pathway mediates embryonic tissue morphogenesis, reproduction and adult tissue regeneration are largely unknown.
source: Wnt5a-Ror signaling constitutes a developmental pathway crucial for embryonic tissue morphogenesis, reproduction and adult tissue regeneration, yet the molecular mechanisms by which the Wnt5a-Ror pathway mediates these processes are largely unknown.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap in the field, representing established scientific consensus about what is not yet understood.

claim: Kif26b was identified as a downstream target of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway through a proteomic screen.
source: Using a proteomic screen, we identify the kinesin superfamily protein Kif26b as a downstream target of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the phosphoproteomic screen described in the manuscript.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror regulates the cellular stability of Kif26b by inducing its degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: Wnt5a-Ror, through a process independent of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin-dependent pathway, regulates the cellular stability of Kif26b by inducing its degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Wnt5a-induced Kif26b degradation that is blocked by proteasome and ubiquitin inhibitors.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror regulation of Kif26b occurs through a process independent of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin-dependent pathway.
source: Wnt5a-Ror, through a process independent of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin-dependent pathway, regulates the cellular stability of Kif26b by inducing its degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that Dkk-1 and IWR-1, inhibitors of canonical Wnt signaling, do not block Wnt5a-induced Kif26b degradation.

claim: Kif26b modulates the migratory behavior of cultured mesenchymal cells in a Wnt5a-dependent manner.
source: Through this mechanism, Kif26b modulates the migratory behavior of cultured mesenchymal cells in a Wnt5a-dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by wound-healing assay data showing that Kif26b levels affect cell migration and that Wnt5a treatment modulates this effect.

claim: Genetic perturbation of Kif26b function in vivo causes embryonic axis malformations in zebrafish.
source: Genetic perturbation of Kif26b function in vivo caused embryonic axis malformations and depletion of primordial germ cells in the developing gonad, two phenotypes characteristic of disrupted Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from zebrafish embryo microinjection experiments showing axis truncation and bending phenotypes.

claim: Genetic perturbation of Kif26b function in vivo causes depletion of primordial germ cells in the developing gonad.
source: Genetic perturbation of Kif26b function in vivo caused embryonic axis malformations and depletion of primordial germ cells in the developing gonad, two phenotypes characteristic of disrupted Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Kif26b knockout mouse embryos showing reduced PGC numbers in gonads.

claim: Embryonic axis malformations and depletion of primordial germ cells in the developing gonad are phenotypes characteristic of disrupted Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
source: Genetic perturbation of Kif26b function in vivo caused embryonic axis malformations and depletion of primordial germ cells in the developing gonad, two phenotypes characteristic of disrupted Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
evidence: This draws on established knowledge from previous studies of Wnt5a and Ror mutants, as cited throughout the manuscript.

claim: Kif26b links Wnt5a-Ror signaling to the control of morphogenetic cell and tissue behaviors in vertebrates.
source: These findings indicate that Kif26b links Wnt5a-Ror signaling to the control of morphogenetic cell and tissue behaviors in vertebrates and reveal a new role for regulated proteolysis in noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror signal transduction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined experimental data showing Kif26b regulation by Wnt5a-Ror and its effects on cell migration and development.

claim: Regulated proteolysis plays a role in noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror signal transduction.
source: These findings indicate that Kif26b links Wnt5a-Ror signaling to the control of morphogenetic cell and tissue behaviors in vertebrates and reveal a new role for regulated proteolysis in noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror signal transduction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation of Kif26b in response to Wnt5a-Ror signaling.

claim: Wnt ligands achieve high functional versatility in part by activating multiple biochemically distinct pathways to regulate diverse cell biological processes.
source: Wnt ligands achieve high functional versatility in part by activating multiple biochemically distinct pathways to regulate diverse cell biological processes (Veeman et al., 2003; Semenov et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature establishing this concept.

claim: The canonical Wnt pathway signals through the transcription co-regulator β-catenin to induce target gene expression.
source: Unlike the well-characterized 'canonical' Wnt pathway that signals through the transcription co-regulator β-catenin to induce target gene expression, a subset of Wnts signal independently of this Wnt/β-catenin pathway via 'noncanonical' mechanisms to control cytoskeleton-driven morphogenetic events such as directed cell movements, changes in cell polarization and cell adhesion (Moon et al., 1993; Veeman et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the cited references.

claim: A subset of Wnts signal independently of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway via noncanonical mechanisms to control cytoskeleton-driven morphogenetic events such as directed cell movements, changes in cell polarization and cell adhesion.
source: Unlike the well-characterized 'canonical' Wnt pathway that signals through the transcription co-regulator β-catenin to induce target gene expression, a subset of Wnts signal independently of this Wnt/β-catenin pathway via 'noncanonical' mechanisms to control cytoskeleton-driven morphogenetic events such as directed cell movements, changes in cell polarization and cell adhesion (Moon et al., 1993; Veeman et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the cited references.

claim: Wnt5a is critical for the proper morphogenesis of many tissues throughout the developing embryo.
source: The best-studied noncanonical Wnt, Wnt5a, is critical for the proper morphogenesis of many tissues throughout the developing embryo (Moon et al., 1993; Yamaguchi et al., 1999; Bodmer et al., 2009; Laird et al., 2011; Chawengsaksophak et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2012; Cha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Dysregulation of Wnt5a signaling leads to birth defects.
source: Dysregulation of Wnt5a signaling leads to birth defects and is associated with multiple pathological processes in the adult including cancer metastasis and inflammatory diseases such as atherosclerosis (Kurayoshi et al., 2006; Da Forno et al., 2008; Yamamoto et al., 2010; Jin et al., 2012; Lu et al., 2012; Bhatt and Malgor, 2014; Ford et al., 2014; Lin et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Qin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the cited references.

claim: Dysregulation of Wnt5a signaling is associated with cancer metastasis.
source: Dysregulation of Wnt5a signaling leads to birth defects and is associated with multiple pathological processes in the adult including cancer metastasis and inflammatory diseases such as atherosclerosis (Kurayoshi et al., 2006; Da Forno et al., 2008; Yamamoto et al., 2010; Jin et al., 2012; Lu et al., 2012; Bhatt and Malgor, 2014; Ford et al., 2014; Lin et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Qin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the cited references.

claim: Dysregulation of Wnt5a signaling is associated with inflammatory diseases such as atherosclerosis.
source: Dysregulation of Wnt5a signaling leads to birth defects and is associated with multiple pathological processes in the adult including cancer metastasis and inflammatory diseases such as atherosclerosis (Kurayoshi et al., 2006; Da Forno et al., 2008; Yamamoto et al., 2010; Jin et al., 2012; Lu et al., 2012; Bhatt and Malgor, 2014; Ford et al., 2014; Lin et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Qin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the cited references.

claim: The Ror family of receptor tyrosine kinases mediates Wnt5a-dependent morphogenetic functions in the developing animal.
source: A growing consensus suggests that the Ror family of receptor tyrosine kinases mediates Wnt5a-dependent morphogenetic functions in the developing animal (Oishi et al., 2003; Green et al., 2008a; Mikels et al., 2009; Ho et al., 2012).
evidence: This represents a growing consensus in the field, supported by the cited references.

claim: How Wnt5a signaling via Ror receptors affects downstream cellular processes remains poorly understood.
source: However, how Wnt5a signaling via Ror receptors affects downstream cellular processes remains poorly understood.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Among the many biochemical activities previously proposed to be downstream of Wnt5a signaling, only the phosphorylation of Dishevelled (Dvl) required the expression of both Wnt5a and Ror proteins.
source: In a previous study, we found that among the many biochemical activities previously proposed to be downstream of Wnt5a signaling, only the phosphorylation of the cytoplasmic scaffolding protein Dishevelled (Dvl) required the expression of both Wnt5a and Ror proteins (Ho et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by data from a previous study by the authors, as indicated by the citation.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror-dependent phosphorylation of Dvl specifically mediates the biological functions of Wnt5a signaling.
source: This finding suggested that Wnt5a-Ror-dependent phosphorylation of Dvl specifically mediates the biological functions of Wnt5a signaling and led us to propose that Ror and Dvl are key components of the noncanonical Wnt5a pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the previous finding about Dvl phosphorylation.

claim: Ror and Dvl are key components of the noncanonical Wnt5a pathway.
source: This finding suggested that Wnt5a-Ror-dependent phosphorylation of Dvl specifically mediates the biological functions of Wnt5a signaling and led us to propose that Ror and Dvl are key components of the noncanonical Wnt5a pathway.
evidence: This is a proposal based on inference from previous experimental findings.

claim: Human mutations in WNT5A, ROR2, DVL1 and DVL3 can cause Robinow syndrome.
source: The assignment of these proteins to a common pathway is further supported by the observation that human mutations in WNT5A, ROR2, DVL1 and DVL3 can cause Robinow syndrome, a congenital disorder characterized by short-limbed dwarfism and morphological defects in craniofacial and genital structures, demonstrating that the Wnt5a-Ror-Dvl pathway regulates morphogenesis during human development (Afzal et al., 2000; van Bokhoven et al., 2000; Person et al., 2010; Bunn et al., 2015; White et al., 2015, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from human genetics studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: Robinow syndrome is a congenital disorder characterized by short-limbed dwarfism and morphological defects in craniofacial and genital structures.
source: The assignment of these proteins to a common pathway is further supported by the observation that human mutations in WNT5A, ROR2, DVL1 and DVL3 can cause Robinow syndrome, a congenital disorder characterized by short-limbed dwarfism and morphological defects in craniofacial and genital structures, demonstrating that the Wnt5a-Ror-Dvl pathway regulates morphogenesis during human development (Afzal et al., 2000; van Bokhoven et al., 2000; Person et al., 2010; Bunn et al., 2015; White et al., 2015, 2016).
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about Robinow syndrome.

claim: The Wnt5a-Ror-Dvl pathway regulates morphogenesis during human development.
source: The assignment of these proteins to a common pathway is further supported by the observation that human mutations in WNT5A, ROR2, DVL1 and DVL3 can cause Robinow syndrome, a congenital disorder characterized by short-limbed dwarfism and morphological defects in craniofacial and genital structures, demonstrating that the Wnt5a-Ror-Dvl pathway regulates morphogenesis during human development (Afzal et al., 2000; van Bokhoven et al., 2000; Person et al., 2010; Bunn et al., 2015; White et al., 2015, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genetic evidence linking mutations in these genes to Robinow syndrome.

claim: The function of Dvl phosphorylation is not clear.
source: However, since the function of Dvl phosphorylation is not clear, and Dvl is a common component of several signaling pathways including the canonical Wnt signaling pathway and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway, how the Wnt5a-Ror pathway signals to carry out its biological functions remains incompletely understood.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Dvl is a common component of several signaling pathways including the canonical Wnt signaling pathway and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway.
source: However, since the function of Dvl phosphorylation is not clear, and Dvl is a common component of several signaling pathways including the canonical Wnt signaling pathway and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway, how the Wnt5a-Ror pathway signals to carry out its biological functions remains incompletely understood.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Dvl function in multiple signaling pathways.

claim: A whole phosphoproteome-scale mass spectrometric screen was conducted comparing wild-type cells with cells lacking the Ror family of proteins.
source: In this study, we conducted a whole phosphoproteome-scale mass spectrometric screen comparing wild-type cells with cells lacking the Ror family of proteins in an effort to identify additional effectors of Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The phosphoproteomic screen identified a number of candidate proteins whose levels or phosphorylation status was influenced by Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
source: The screen identified a number of candidate proteins whose levels or phosphorylation status was influenced by Wnt5a-Ror signaling, including factors involved in cytoskeletal regulation and cell adhesion, processes crucial for the morphogenesis of tissues.
evidence: This is supported by the data from the phosphoproteomic screen.

claim: The phosphoproteomic screen identified factors involved in cytoskeletal regulation and cell adhesion.
source: The screen identified a number of candidate proteins whose levels or phosphorylation status was influenced by Wnt5a-Ror signaling, including factors involved in cytoskeletal regulation and cell adhesion, processes crucial for the morphogenesis of tissues.
evidence: This is supported by the data from the phosphoproteomic screen.

claim: Cytoskeletal regulation and cell adhesion are processes crucial for the morphogenesis of tissues.
source: The screen identified a number of candidate proteins whose levels or phosphorylation status was influenced by Wnt5a-Ror signaling, including factors involved in cytoskeletal regulation and cell adhesion, processes crucial for the morphogenesis of tissues.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: Mutations in the C. elegans orthologs of Ror and Kif26b produce similar neuronal migration and axon guidance phenotypes.
source: Mutations in the C. elegans orthologs of Ror and Kif26b produce similar neuronal migration and axon guidance phenotypes, suggesting that these molecules might function in a common molecular pathway (Wightman et al., 1996; Forrester et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from C. elegans genetics studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: The similar phenotypes of C. elegans Ror and Kif26b orthologs suggest that these molecules might function in a common molecular pathway.
source: Mutations in the C. elegans orthologs of Ror and Kif26b produce similar neuronal migration and axon guidance phenotypes, suggesting that these molecules might function in a common molecular pathway (Wightman et al., 1996; Forrester et al., 1998).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similar phenotypes observed in C. elegans mutants.

claim: Kif26b plays crucial roles in regulating cytoskeleton-driven processes, including cell migration, polarization and adhesion.
source: Moreover, recent studies demonstrated that Kif26b plays crucial roles in regulating cytoskeleton-driven processes, including cell migration, polarization and adhesion, raising the possibility that Kif26b could function specifically as a cytoskeletal effector of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway (Uchiyama et al., 2010; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from recent studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: Kif26b could function specifically as a cytoskeletal effector of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway.
source: Moreover, recent studies demonstrated that Kif26b plays crucial roles in regulating cytoskeleton-driven processes, including cell migration, polarization and adhesion, raising the possibility that Kif26b could function specifically as a cytoskeletal effector of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway (Uchiyama et al., 2010; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculation based on the known functions of Kif26b and the Wnt5a-Ror pathway.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling regulates the steady-state abundance of Kif26b in cells via a mechanism involving the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: Through a series of biochemical studies, we demonstrate that Wnt5a-Ror signaling regulates the steady-state abundance of Kif26b in cells via a mechanism involving the ubiquitin-proteasome system that is independent of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin-dependent pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Wnt5a-induced Kif26b degradation blocked by proteasome and ubiquitin inhibitors.

claim: Gain- and loss-of-function experiments in cultured mesenchymal cells indicate that Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling modulates mesenchymal cell migration.
source: Importantly, gain- and loss-of-function experiments in cultured mesenchymal cells indicate that Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling modulates mesenchymal cell migration.
evidence: This is supported by wound-healing assay data with Kif26b overexpression and knockout cell lines.

claim: Perturbation of Kif26b function disrupts a number of Wnt5a/Ror-dependent processes in vivo.
source: We also find that perturbation of Kif26b function disrupts a number of Wnt5a/Ror-dependent processes in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo data from zebrafish and mouse experiments.

claim: Mis-expression of Kif26b in developing zebrafish embryos causes axis and craniofacial malformations.
source: For example, in developing zebrafish embryos, mis-expression of Kif26b causes axis and craniofacial malformations, thus mirroring the effects of mis-expression of Wnt5a or Ror in zebrafish.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from zebrafish microinjection experiments.

claim: Mis-expression of Kif26b in zebrafish mirrors the effects of mis-expression of Wnt5a or Ror in zebrafish.
source: For example, in developing zebrafish embryos, mis-expression of Kif26b causes axis and craniofacial malformations, thus mirroring the effects of mis-expression of Wnt5a or Ror in zebrafish.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the phenotypes of Kif26b, Wnt5a, and Ror mis-expression.

claim: Kif26b expression is required for primordial germ cells to populate the developing gonad in mouse embryos.
source: In developing mouse embryos, Kif26b expression is required for primordial germ cells to populate the developing gonad, a process that also requires the expression of Wnt5a or Ror proteins.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing reduced PGC numbers in Kif26b knockout mouse gonads.

claim: Primordial germ cell colonization of the developing gonad requires the expression of Wnt5a or Ror proteins.
source: In developing mouse embryos, Kif26b expression is required for primordial germ cells to populate the developing gonad, a process that also requires the expression of Wnt5a or Ror proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, as cited elsewhere in the manuscript.

claim: Kif26b functions as a downstream effector of the noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror pathway that regulates cell and tissue behaviors during development.
source: Taken together, these findings establish Kif26b as a downstream effector of the noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror pathway that regulates cell and tissue behaviors during development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined experimental data presented in the study.

claim: 6498 unique phosphopeptides, representing 7426 distinct phosphosites, were quantified in the phosphoproteomic screen.
source: 6498 unique phosphopeptides, representing 7426 distinct phosphosites, were quantified in the screen (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is data from the mass spectrometry screen.

claim: Fifteen unique phosphopeptides were identified as hits in the phosphoproteomic screen.
source: A total of fifteen unique phosphopeptides were identified as hits (Figure 1B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is data from the mass spectrometry screen, also shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Eleven phosphopeptides increased in abundance and four phosphopeptides decreased in abundance upon Ror depletion.
source: Eleven phosphopeptides increased in abundance and four phosphopeptides decreased in abundance upon Ror depletion.
evidence: This is data from the mass spectrometry screen.

claim: Eight of the phosphopeptides that increased in abundance upon Ror depletion mapped to Kif26b.
source: Eight of the phosphopeptides that increased in abundance mapped to the same protein—the kinesin superfamily member Kif26b—making it a high-confidence candidate target of Wnt5a-Ror signaling (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is data from the mass spectrometry screen, shown in Figure 1B, 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: All eight Kif26b phosphopeptides exhibited a significant increase in abundance following genetic ablation of Ror expression in both experimental replicates.
source: Moreover, all eight Kif26b phosphopeptides exhibited a significant increase in abundance following genetic ablation of Ror expression in both experimental replicates (Figure 1B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is data from the mass spectrometry screen, shown in Figure 1B and Supplementary file 2.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to a decrease in the level of Kif26b protein expression.
source: Taken together, these observations strongly suggest that Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to a decrease in the level of Kif26b protein expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mass spectrometry data showing increased Kif26b phosphopeptides upon Ror depletion.

claim: Kif26b is a highly conserved atypical kinesin of the Kinesin-11 family.
source: Kif26b is a highly conserved atypical kinesin of the Kinesin-11 family, which includes Kif26a and Kif26b, two proteins whose developmental and cellular functions have only begun to be revealed in recent years (Uchiyama et al., 2010; Hirokawa and Tanaka, 2015; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kif26b, supported by the cited references.

claim: The Kinesin-11 family includes Kif26a and Kif26b.
source: Kif26b is a highly conserved atypical kinesin of the Kinesin-11 family, which includes Kif26a and Kif26b, two proteins whose developmental and cellular functions have only begun to be revealed in recent years (Uchiyama et al., 2010; Hirokawa and Tanaka, 2015; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Kinesin-11 family.

claim: The developmental and cellular functions of Kif26a and Kif26b have only begun to be revealed in recent years.
source: Kif26b is a highly conserved atypical kinesin of the Kinesin-11 family, which includes Kif26a and Kif26b, two proteins whose developmental and cellular functions have only begun to be revealed in recent years (Uchiyama et al., 2010; Hirokawa and Tanaka, 2015; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, supported by the cited references.

claim: Kif26b levels were elevated in Ror1f/f; Ror2f/f; CAG-CreER MEFs treated with 4-OHT as compared to MEFs with the same genotype treated with a vehicle control.
source: We found that Kif26b levels were elevated in Ror1f/f; Ror2f/f; CAG-CreER MEFs treated with 4-OHT as compared to MEFs with the same genotype treated with a vehicle control (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling negatively regulates total Kif26b protein expression.
source: This finding suggests that Wnt5a-Ror signaling negatively regulates total Kif26b protein expression, as opposed to selectively catalyzing the dephosphorylation of multiple phosphorylation sites across the Kif26b protein.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the western blot data showing elevated Kif26b levels upon Ror depletion.

claim: Wnt5a-/- MEFs had a higher level of Kif26b protein relative to wild-type control MEFs.
source: We observed that Wnt5a-/- MEFs also had a higher level of Kif26b protein relative to wild-type control MEFs, indicating that Wnt5a, like Ror1 and Ror2, negatively regulates the steady-state level of Kif26b expression (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Wnt5a negatively regulates the steady-state level of Kif26b expression.
source: We observed that Wnt5a-/- MEFs also had a higher level of Kif26b protein relative to wild-type control MEFs, indicating that Wnt5a, like Ror1 and Ror2, negatively regulates the steady-state level of Kif26b expression (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the western blot data comparing Wnt5a-/- and wild-type MEFs.

claim: Wnt5a signaling via Ror proteins leads to a decrease in Kif26b protein expression.
source: This finding suggests that Wnt5a signaling via Ror proteins leads to a decrease in Kif26b protein expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data showing elevated Kif26b in both Ror and Wnt5a knockout MEFs.

claim: Treatment of Wnt5a-/- MEFs with purified, recombinant Wnt5a led to a decrease in Kif26b protein expression in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We stimulated Wnt5a-/- MEFs with purified, recombinant Wnt5a and found that this treatment led to a decrease in Kif26b protein expression in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The decrease in Kif26b upon Wnt5a treatment was accompanied by a commensurate increase in Ror1 and Dvl2 phosphorylation.
source: The decrease in Kif26b was accompanied by a commensurate increase in Ror1 and Dvl2 phosphorylation, a readout of Wnt5a-Ror signaling (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Wnt5a induces the downregulation of endogenous Kif26b expression as the Wnt5a-Ror-Dvl pathway becomes activated.
source: These findings suggest that Wnt5a induces the downregulation of endogenous Kif26b expression as the Wnt5a-Ror-Dvl pathway becomes activated.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation between Kif26b downregulation and Ror1/Dvl2 phosphorylation.

claim: Wnt5a-induced downregulation of Kif26b is first detected 1 hr after Wnt5a stimulation and is maximally decreased after 6 hr.
source: We found that the Wnt5a-induced downregulation of Kif26b expression is first detected 1 hr after Wnt5a stimulation and that Kif26b expression is maximally decreased after 6 hr (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by time-course western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The kinetics of Kif26b protein downregulation closely paralleled those of Ror1 and Dvl2 phosphorylation in response to acute Wnt5a stimulation.
source: The kinetics of Kif26b protein downregulation closely paralleled those of Ror1 and Dvl2 phosphorylation in response to acute Wnt5a stimulation (Figure 2D), suggesting that Wnt5a signaling regulates these downstream biochemical events in a coordinated manner.
evidence: This is supported by time-course western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Wnt5a signaling regulates Kif26b downregulation and Ror1/Dvl2 phosphorylation in a coordinated manner.
source: The kinetics of Kif26b protein downregulation closely paralleled those of Ror1 and Dvl2 phosphorylation in response to acute Wnt5a stimulation (Figure 2D), suggesting that Wnt5a signaling regulates these downstream biochemical events in a coordinated manner.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similar kinetics of Kif26b downregulation and Ror1/Dvl2 phosphorylation.

claim: Stimulation with Wnt5a does not change the level of Kif26b mRNA in Wnt5a-/- MEFs.
source: In addition, we found that stimulation with Wnt5a does not change the level of Kif26b mRNA in Wnt5a-/- MEFs, as assayed by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), throughout the course of the experiment (Figure 2E), suggesting that Wnt5a-dependent downregulation of Kif26b protein levels occurs post-transcriptionally.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Wnt5a-dependent downregulation of Kif26b protein levels occurs post-transcriptionally.
source: In addition, we found that stimulation with Wnt5a does not change the level of Kif26b mRNA in Wnt5a-/- MEFs, as assayed by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), throughout the course of the experiment (Figure 2E), suggesting that Wnt5a-dependent downregulation of Kif26b protein levels occurs post-transcriptionally.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Kif26b mRNA levels do not change upon Wnt5a stimulation.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to a decrease in the steady-state levels of Kif26b protein expression in MEFs.
source: Together, these findings establish that Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to a decrease in the steady-state levels of Kif26b protein expression in MEFs and validate Kif26b as a bona fide target of the Wnt5a-Ror signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data presented.

claim: Kif26b is a bona fide target of the Wnt5a-Ror signaling pathway.
source: Together, these findings establish that Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to a decrease in the steady-state levels of Kif26b protein expression in MEFs and validate Kif26b as a bona fide target of the Wnt5a-Ror signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data presented.

claim: The Wnt5a-Ror pathway is generally thought to operate via a noncanonical, β-catenin-independent mechanism.
source: The Wnt5a-Ror pathway is generally thought to operate via a noncanonical, β-catenin-independent mechanism (Green et al., 2008b).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Dkk-1 is an antagonist of the β-catenin-dependent Wnt pathway that binds and prevents the phosphorylation of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway co-receptors Lrp5 and Lrp6.
source: To determine whether Wnt5a-Ror signaling induces the downregulation of Kif26b expression via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism, we tested whether blocking the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway with Dkk-1, an antagonist of the β-catenin-dependent Wnt pathway that binds and prevents the phosphorylation of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway co-receptors Lrp5 and Lrp6, inhibits the Wnt5a-induced decrease in Kif26b protein in MEFs (Bafico et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Dkk-1 function, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Exposure of Wnt5a-/- MEFs to exogenous Wnt5a protein induced Kif26b downregulation to a similar degree with and without the addition of Dkk-1.
source: We found that exposure of Wnt5a-/- MEFs to exogenous Wnt5a protein induced Kif26b downregulation to a similar degree with and without the addition of Dkk-1 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Dkk-1 completely blocked Wnt3a-dependent phosphorylation of Lrp6.
source: To ensure that the Dkk-1 protein used in the experiment was active, we assessed whether the same concentration of Dkk-1 was capable of blocking signaling by Wnt3a, a prototypic canonical Wnt that induces the phosphorylation of the Wnt receptor Lrp6. We found that Wnt3a-dependent phosphorylation of Lrp6 was completely blocked in the presence of Dkk-1 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Wnt5a-dependent regulation of Kif26b occurs via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism that is independent of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
source: These findings suggest that Wnt5a-dependent regulation of Kif26b occurs via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism that is independent of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Dkk-1 does not block Wnt5a-induced Kif26b downregulation.

claim: IWR-1 is a small molecule that inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling by stabilizing Axin2.
source: To verify that Wnt5a regulation of Kif26b occurs via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism, we next tested whether inhibiting the Wnt/β-catenin pathway at a more downstream step blocks Wnt5a-dependent downregulation of Kif26b levels. For this purpose, we used IWR-1, a small molecule that inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling by stabilizing Axin2, a key component of the β-catenin destruction complex (Lee et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about IWR-1 function, supported by the cited references.

claim: Axin2 is a key component of the β-catenin destruction complex.
source: To verify that Wnt5a regulation of Kif26b occurs via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism, we next tested whether inhibiting the Wnt/β-catenin pathway at a more downstream step blocks Wnt5a-dependent downregulation of Kif26b levels. For this purpose, we used IWR-1, a small molecule that inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling by stabilizing Axin2, a key component of the β-catenin destruction complex (Lee et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the β-catenin destruction complex.

claim: Pre-treatment of Wnt5a-/- MEFs with IWR-1 did not block the ability of Wnt5a or Wnt3a to induce the downregulation of Kif26b protein expression.
source: Similar to our findings using Dkk-1 to block the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway at the receptor level, we found that pre-treatment of Wnt5a-/- MEFs with IWR-1 did not block the ability of Wnt5a or Wnt3a to induce the downregulation of Kif26b protein expression (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to the downregulation of Kif26b protein expression via a noncanonical, β-catenin-independent mechanism.
source: These results further support the conclusion that Wnt5a-Ror signaling leads to the downregulation of Kif26b protein expression via a noncanonical, β-catenin-independent mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data with Dkk-1 and IWR-1 inhibitors.

claim: The addition of exogenous Wnt3a protein led to a decrease in the expression of Kif26b in Wnt5a-/- MEFs, even in the presence of Dkk-1 or IWR-1.
source: It is interesting to note that the addition of exogenous Wnt3a protein, classically considered a canonical Wnt, also led to a decrease in the expression of Kif26b in Wnt5a-/- MEFs, even in the presence of Dkk-1 or IWR-1 (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figures 2F and 2G.

claim: Exogenous Wnt3a signals via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism to downregulate the expression of Kif26b.
source: These findings indicate that exogenous Wnt3a also signals via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism to downregulate the expression of Kif26b and supports the emerging view that the distinction between canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling is not strictly determined at the level of Wnt ligands (van Amerongen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Wnt3a can induce Kif26b downregulation independently of canonical Wnt signaling.

claim: The distinction between canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling is not strictly determined at the level of Wnt ligands.
source: These findings indicate that exogenous Wnt3a also signals via a noncanonical Wnt signaling mechanism to downregulate the expression of Kif26b and supports the emerging view that the distinction between canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling is not strictly determined at the level of Wnt ligands (van Amerongen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an emerging view in the field, supported by the cited reference and the data presented.

claim: There may be specificity to Wnt3a and Wnt5a signaling in the developing embryo that is lost when these factors are studied using cultured MEFs.
source: However, it is also possible that there is some specificity to Wnt3a and Wnt5a signaling in the developing embryo that is lost when these factors are studied using cultured MEFs.
evidence: This is speculation about potential differences between in vitro and in vivo contexts.

claim: Wnt5a treatment leads to a decrease in Kif26b expression by promoting Kif26b turnover.
source: Consistent with the hypothesis that Wnt5a treatment leads to the increased degradation of Kif26b, we found that Wnt5a accelerated the turnover of GFP-Kif26b in the reporter cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the absence of Wnt5a stimulation, 80.2% of the GFP-Kif26b signal remained in cells 6 hr after cycloheximide treatment.
source: In the absence of Wnt5a stimulation, 80.2% of the GFP-Kif26b signal remained in the cells 6 hr after the initiation of the cycloheximide treatment.
evidence: This is data from the cycloheximide chase experiment.

claim: In the presence of Wnt5a stimulation, only 33.2% of the GFP-Kif26b signal remained 6 hr after cycloheximide treatment.
source: By contrast, in the presence of Wnt5a stimulation, only 33.2% of the GFP-Kif26b signal remained in the same period.
evidence: This is data from the cycloheximide chase experiment.

claim: Wnt5a treatment leads to a decrease in the steady-state levels of Kif26b expression in cells by promoting Kif26b turnover.
source: These results strongly suggest that Wnt5a treatment leads to a decrease in the steady-state levels of Kif26b expression in cells by promoting Kif26b turnover.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cycloheximide chase data.

claim: Pre-treatment of the WRK reporter line with epoxomicin strongly blocked Wnt5a-induced Kif26b downregulation.
source: Pre-treatment of the WRK reporter line with epoxomicin strongly blocked Wnt5a-induced Kif26b downregulation (Figure 3D,F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3D and 3F.

claim: Wnt5a-induced downregulation of Kif26b occurs via proteasome-dependent degradation.
source: This result suggests that Wnt5a-induced downregulation of Kif26b occurs via proteasome-dependent degradation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the epoxomicin inhibitor data.

claim: Pre-treatment of the WRK reporter cells with PYR-41 blocked Wnt5a-induced Kif26b downregulation to an extent similar to that observed upon epoxomicin treatment.
source: Pre-treatment of the WRK reporter cells with PYR-41 blocked Wnt5a-induced Kif26b downregulation to an extent similar to that observed upon epoxomicin treatment (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: Downregulation of Kif26b expression induced by Wnt5a occurs via the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: This finding provides further evidence that downregulation of Kif26b expression induced by Wnt5a occurs via the UPS.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data with epoxomicin and PYR-41 inhibitors.

claim: Exposure to Wnt5a leads to the downregulation of the steady-state levels of Kif26b expression by promoting Kif26b ubiquitin- and proteasome-dependent degradation.
source: We conclude from these results that exposure to Wnt5a leads to the downregulation of the steady-state levels of Kif26b expression by promoting Kif26b ubiquitin- and proteasome-dependent degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined inhibitor data.

claim: Fzd proteins function as co-receptors in canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling and as polarity determinants in the PCP pathway.
source: Fzds make up a family of 10 seven-transmembrane domain receptor proteins that function as co-receptors in canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling and as polarity determinants in the PCP pathway (Vinson and Adler, 1987; Bhanot et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Fzd function, supported by the cited references.

claim: Recent work implicates Fzd proteins in aspects of noncanonical Wnt function as well as in the phosphorylation of Ror2 in cultured cells.
source: Recent work additionally implicates Fzd proteins in aspects of noncanonical Wnt function as well as in the phosphorylation of Ror2 in cultured cells (Habas et al., 2001; Nishita et al., 2010; Grumolato et al., 2010; Sato et al., 2010).
evidence: This is recent knowledge from the field, supported by the cited references.

claim: Fzd1, Fzd2 and Fzd7 form a distinct sub-family that functions redundantly to control tissue morphogenetic events such as convergent extension of embryonic tissues and closure of the palate and ventricular septum.
source: Moreover, protein sequence homology analysis and in vivo mouse genetic studies revealed that Fzd1, Fzd2 and Fzd7 form a distinct sub-family that functions redundantly to control tissue morphogenetic events such as convergent extension of embryonic tissues and closure of the palate and ventricular septum (Yu et al., 2010; Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from mouse genetics studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: Many developmental processes that require Fzd1, Fzd2 and Fzd7 also require the Wnt5a-Ror pathway.
source: As many of these developmental processes also require the Wnt5a-Ror pathway, we hypothesized that certain Fzd proteins, such as those in the Fzd1, Fzd2 and Fzd7 sub-family, might participate in Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the overlap in developmental processes requiring Fzds and Wnt5a-Ror.

claim: Certain Fzd proteins, such as those in the Fzd1, Fzd2 and Fzd7 sub-family, might participate in Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling.
source: As many of these developmental processes also require the Wnt5a-Ror pathway, we hypothesized that certain Fzd proteins, such as those in the Fzd1, Fzd2 and Fzd7 sub-family, might participate in Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the overlap in developmental processes.

claim: Shisa proteins are Wnt signaling regulators that inhibit Fzd processing and trafficking by sequestering Fzds in the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: To test whether Fzd proteins mediate Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling, we first took a loss-of-function approach using Shisa proteins, which are Wnt signaling regulators that inhibit Fzd processing and trafficking by sequestering Fzds in the endoplasmic reticulum (Yamamoto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Shisa protein function, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Viral transduction of Shisa2 expression partially blocked the ability of Wnt5a to induce Kif26b degradation in the WRK reporter cell line.
source: We found that viral transduction of Shisa2 expression, but not Cas9 expression as a control, partially blocked the ability of Wnt5a to induce Kif26b degradation in the WRK reporter cell line (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: The Fzd family plays a role in Wnt5a-dependent regulation of Kif26b.
source: This observation suggests that the Fzd family plays a role in Wnt5a-dependent regulation of Kif26b.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Shisa2 inhibition data.

claim: Lentiviral transduction of Fzd1 or Fzd7 expression constitutively induced Kif26b degradation as measured in the WRK assay.
source: Interestingly, we found that lentiviral transduction of Fzd1 or Fzd7 expression, but not of the negative control Cas9, constitutively induced Kif26b degradation as measured in the WRK assay (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: Fzd family proteins are involved in Wnt5a regulation of Kif26b degradation, possibly as co-receptors together with members of the Ror family of proteins.
source: This finding, taken together with the decreased Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling upon expression of the Fzd inhibitor Shisa2, strongly suggests that Fzd family proteins are involved in Wnt5a regulation of Kif26b degradation, possibly as co-receptors together with members of the Ror family of proteins.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined Shisa2 and Fzd overexpression data.

claim: All the Fzd family members tested were able to induce Kif26b degradation.
source: Interestingly, we found that all the Fzd family members that we tested were able to induce Kif26b degradation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The specificity of Fzd protein function may be lost when these proteins are overexpressed.
source: However, it is possible that the specificity of Fzd protein function is lost when these proteins are overexpressed.
evidence: This is speculation about potential artifacts of overexpression experiments.

claim: Dvl phosphorylation is a specific downstream target of Wnt5a-Ror signaling.
source: Our previous study identified Dvl phosphorylation as a specific downstream target of Wnt5a-Ror signaling (Ho et al., 2012), and a recent study demonstrated that the Dvl and Kif26b proteins physically interact (Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: The Dvl and Kif26b proteins physically interact.
source: Our previous study identified Dvl phosphorylation as a specific downstream target of Wnt5a-Ror signaling (Ho et al., 2012), and a recent study demonstrated that the Dvl and Kif26b proteins physically interact (Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a recent study, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Wnt5a-induced Kif26b degradation occurs with similar kinetics as Wnt5a-induced Dvl phosphorylation.
source: Moreover, we found that Wnt5a-induced Kif26b degradation occurs with similar kinetics as Wnt5a-induced Dvl phosphorylation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by time-course western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Overexpression of Dvl1 led to an increase in Kif26b degradation.
source: Using the WRK reporter assay, we found that overexpression of Dvl1, but not overexpression of a control protein Cas9, led to an increase in Kif26b degradation (Figure 4E,F), mimicking the effects of Wnt5a stimulation or Fzd overexpression.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: Both Fzd receptors and Dvl1 have a functional role in Wnt5a-Ror-dependent Kif26b degradation.
source: Taken together, these findings establish a functional role for both Fzd receptors and Dvl1 (and likely other Dvl proteins) in Wnt5a-Ror-dependent Kif26b degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined Fzd and Dvl overexpression data.

claim: Mutations in the nematode orthologs of Kif26b (vab-8) and Ror (cam-1) cause similar polarized cell migration and axon guidance phenotypes in C. elegans.
source: Genetic studies in C. elegans have shown that mutations in the nematode orthologs of Kif26b (vab-8) and Ror (cam-1) cause similar polarized cell migration and axon guidance phenotypes, and a recent study in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) demonstrates a physical interaction between Kif26b and Dvl3 (Forrester et al., 1998; Wolf et al., 1998; Chien et al., 2015; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from C. elegans genetics studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: A recent study in HUVECs demonstrates a physical interaction between Kif26b and Dvl3.
source: Genetic studies in C. elegans have shown that mutations in the nematode orthologs of Kif26b (vab-8) and Ror (cam-1) cause similar polarized cell migration and axon guidance phenotypes, and a recent study in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) demonstrates a physical interaction between Kif26b and Dvl3 (Forrester et al., 1998; Wolf et al., 1998; Chien et al., 2015; Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a recent study, supported by the cited references.

claim: The cell biological effects of noncanonical Wnt signaling may be mediated by the Wnt5a-Ror-dependent degradation of Kif26b.
source: These findings, together with the observations reported above, raise the possibility that the cell biological effects of noncanonical Wnt signaling are mediated by the Wnt5a-Ror-dependent degradation of Kif26b.
evidence: This is speculation based on the combined evidence from C. elegans, HUVECs, and the current study.

claim: GFP-tagged Kif26b protein is overexpressed relative to endogenous Kif26b in NIH/3T3 cells.
source: Western analysis of the NIH/3T3 cell lines used in the WRK assay showed that GFP-tagged Kif26b protein is overexpressed relative to endogenous Kif26b in NIH/3T3 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), indicating that these cells could be used to assess the effects of Kif26b overexpression on cell responses.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Neither GFP-Kif26b overexpression nor loss of Kif26b affects cell proliferation or survival.
source: We next confirmed that neither GFP-Kif26b overexpression nor loss of Kif26b affects cell proliferation or survival through mitotic index quantification and TUNEL staining, respectively (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–G), indicating that these NIH/3T3 cell lines could be used to study other possible Kif26b-dependent cellular responses.
evidence: This is supported by mitotic index and TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–G.

claim: Kif26b-knockout cells exhibit a decrease in wound closure efficiency relative to control cells.
source: We found that Kif26b-knockout cells exhibit a decrease in wound closure efficiency relative to control cells while cell lines overexpressing GFP-Kif26b exhibit an enhanced rate of wound closure efficiency relative to control cells (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by wound-healing assay data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Cell lines overexpressing GFP-Kif26b exhibit an enhanced rate of wound closure efficiency relative to control cells.
source: We found that Kif26b-knockout cells exhibit a decrease in wound closure efficiency relative to control cells while cell lines overexpressing GFP-Kif26b exhibit an enhanced rate of wound closure efficiency relative to control cells (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by wound-healing assay data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Kif26b may promote cell migration.
source: These findings suggest that Kif26b may promote cell migration and are consistent with previous observations in HUVECs where Kif26b expression was correlated with increased directional cell migration (Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the wound-healing assay data and previous observations in HUVECs.

claim: In HUVECs, Kif26b expression was correlated with increased directional cell migration.
source: These findings suggest that Kif26b may promote cell migration and are consistent with previous observations in HUVECs where Kif26b expression was correlated with increased directional cell migration (Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by the cited reference.

claim: By controlling the rate of Kif26b protein degradation, Wnt5a-Ror signaling regulates cell migration.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that by controlling the rate of Kif26b protein degradation, Wnt5a-Ror signaling regulates cell migration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined data showing Wnt5a-induced Kif26b degradation and the effects of Kif26b levels on cell migration.

claim: Microinjection of Wnt5a mRNA into one-cell zebrafish embryos caused axis truncation and bending phenotypes.
source: Replicating previous reports (Moon et al., 1993; Bai et al., 2014), microinjection of Wnt5a mRNA caused axis truncation and bending phenotypes (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by zebrafish embryo data shown in Figures 6A and 6B, and replicates previous reports.

claim: Microinjection of Kif26b mRNA into one-cell zebrafish embryos caused axis truncation and bending phenotypes resembling those caused by mis-expression of Wnt5a.
source: Strikingly, microinjection of Kif26b mRNA into one-cell zebrafish embryos also caused axis truncation and bending phenotypes resembling those caused by mis-expression of Wnt5a (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by zebrafish embryo data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: The axis truncation and bending phenotypes produced by Kif26b mis-expression are specific.
source: These phenotypes were rarely observed in uninjected embryos or in embryos injected with a negative control mRNA of similar size, Cas9, indicating that the axis truncation and bending phenotypes produced by Kif26b mis-expression are specific (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by control data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Kif26b specifically affects morphogenetic movements of cells in developing embryos in a manner similar to that of Wnt5a or Ror2.
source: Together, these findings suggest that Kif26b specifically affects morphogenetic movements of cells in developing embryos in a manner similar to that of Wnt5a or Ror2 and support a model whereby Kif26b functions as part of a noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror regulatory cassette that regulates morphogenetic movements during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the zebrafish phenotype data.

claim: Kif26b functions as part of a noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror regulatory cassette that regulates morphogenetic movements during embryogenesis.
source: Together, these findings suggest that Kif26b specifically affects morphogenetic movements of cells in developing embryos in a manner similar to that of Wnt5a or Ror2 and support a model whereby Kif26b functions as part of a noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror regulatory cassette that regulates morphogenetic movements during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined zebrafish and other experimental data.

claim: During mouse embryogenesis, PGCs are specified from the epiblast at ~E7.25 and subsequently migrate through the hindgut and dorsal mesentery to populate the gonadal ridges by E11.5.
source: During mouse embryogenesis, PGCs are specified from the epiblast at ~E7.25 and subsequently migrate through the hindgut and dorsal mesentery to populate the gonadal ridges by E11.5.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PGC development in mice.

claim: PGCs that fail to enter the gonad are eliminated by programmed cell death.
source: PGCs that fail to enter the gonad are eliminated by programmed cell death (McLaren, 2003; Laird et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PGC development, supported by the cited references.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in Wnt5a or Ror2 alleles result in a substantial decrease in the number of PGCs that successfully colonize the gonad at E11.5.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in Wnt5a or Ror2 alleles result in a substantial decrease in the number of PGCs that successfully colonize the gonad at E11.5 as compared to wild-type controls (~75% fewer in Wnt5a and ~50% fewer in Ror2 mutants) (Chawengsaksophak et al., 2012; Laird et al., 2011), indicating that Wnt5a-Ror signaling is required for the proper colonization of the gonadal ridges by migrating PGCs.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling is required for the proper colonization of the gonadal ridges by migrating PGCs.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in Wnt5a or Ror2 alleles result in a substantial decrease in the number of PGCs that successfully colonize the gonad at E11.5 as compared to wild-type controls (~75% fewer in Wnt5a and ~50% fewer in Ror2 mutants) (Chawengsaksophak et al., 2012; Laird et al., 2011), indicating that Wnt5a-Ror signaling is required for the proper colonization of the gonadal ridges by migrating PGCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the PGC phenotypes in Wnt5a and Ror2 mutants.

claim: If Kif26b mediates biological activities of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway during PGC development, genetic perturbation of Kif26b might also disrupt PGC colonization of the gonads.
source: We reasoned that if Kif26b mediates biological activities of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway during PGC development, genetic perturbation of Kif26b might also disrupt PGC colonization of the gonads.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the role of Wnt5a-Ror in PGC development.

claim: The mean number of SSEA1-positive PGCs in the Kif26b-/- gonads was decreased significantly to 44.9% of Kif26b+/+ littermate controls.
source: The mean number of SSEA1-positive PGCs in the Kif26b-/- gonads (372.8 ± 74.95, n=4) was decreased significantly to 44.9% of Kif26b+/+ littermate controls (829.5 ± 88.553, n=2) (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is supported by PGC quantification data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: The relative similarity of the PGC depletion phenotypes observed in E11.5 Kif26b-/-, Ror2-/- and Wnt5a-/- mouse embryos suggest that Kif26b functions in a common signaling pathway with Wnt5a and Ror proteins to orchestrate PGC development.
source: The relative similarity of the PGC depletion phenotypes observed in E11.5 Kif26b-/-, Ror2-/- and Wnt5a-/- mouse embryos suggest that Kif26b functions in a common signaling pathway with Wnt5a and Ror proteins to orchestrate PGC development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the PGC phenotypes in different mutants.

claim: The zebrafish mis-expression analysis and mouse PGC experiment provide in vivo evidence that Kif26b contributes to Wnt5a-Ror signaling in multiple tissues during embryonic development.
source: This experiment, taken together with the mis-expression analysis in zebrafish, provides in vivo evidence that Kif26b contributes to Wnt5a-Ror signaling in multiple tissues during embryonic development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined zebrafish and mouse in vivo data.

claim: Few downstream effectors of the noncanonical Wnt signaling system have been identified and validated in biological systems since the discovery that certain Wnt proteins can signal independently of β-catenin-mediated transcription.
source: Since the seminal discovery that certain Wnt proteins can signal independently of β-catenin-mediated transcription to affect organ and tissue morphogenesis during development (Moon et al., 1993), few downstream effectors of this signaling system have been identified and validated in biological systems.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Ror receptors are essential mediators of a core noncanonical Wnt5a pathway crucial for tissue morphogenesis.
source: In our previous work, we used in vivo mouse genetics to demonstrate that Ror receptors are essential mediators of a core noncanonical Wnt5a pathway crucial for tissue morphogenesis (Ho et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the authors' previous work, supported by the cited reference.

claim: C. elegans orthologs of vab-8 and cam-1 were among the fourteen genes identified in a forward mutagenesis screen for genes required for the directional migration of the C. elegans canal-associated neuron.
source: The first indication that Kif26b may mediate Wnt5a/Ror-dependent developmental processes came from studies in C. elegans. Orthologs of Kif26b (vab-8) and Ror (cam-1) were among the fourteen genes identified in a forward mutagenesis screen for genes required for the directional migration of the C. elegans canal-associated neuron (Forrester et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from C. elegans genetics studies, supported by the cited reference.

claim: C. elegans mutants of vab-8 and cam-1 display similar polarized cell migration and axon guidance defects where cell bodies and axons that normally move specifically toward the posterior end of the body become abnormally anteriorly displaced.
source: C. elegans mutants of vab-8 and cam-1 display similar polarized cell migration and axon guidance defects where cell bodies and axons that normally move specifically toward the posterior end of the body become abnormally anteriorly displaced (Wightman et al., 1996; Forrester et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge from C. elegans genetics studies, supported by the cited references.

claim: Both vab-8 and cam-1 mutants exhibit a lower penetrance withered-tail (Wit) phenotype reminiscent of the posterior A-P body axis truncation phenotype seen in Wnt5a or Ror mutant mice.
source: In addition, both vab-8 and cam-1 mutants exhibit a lower penetrance withered-tail (Wit) phenotype reminiscent of the posterior A-P body axis truncation phenotype seen in Wnt5a or Ror mutant mice (Forrester et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from C. elegans genetics studies, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Wnt5a, Ror and Kif26b proteins may function as part of an evolutionarily conserved pathway that orchestrates morphogenetic processes during the development of tissues.
source: These studies, taken together with the findings in mammalian cells described in this article, suggest that Wnt5a, Ror and Kif26b proteins may function as part of an evolutionarily conserved pathway that orchestrates morphogenetic processes during the development of tissues.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined C. elegans and mammalian data.

claim: A recent study identified Kif26b as a binding partner of Dvl3 in HUVECs.
source: Further evidence suggesting Kif26b may function in noncanonical Wnt signaling came from a recent study that identified Kif26b as a binding partner of Dvl3 in HUVECs (Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016), as Dvl proteins are known targets of Wnt5a-Ror signaling (Ho et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a recent study, supported by the cited reference.

claim: A recent study demonstrated that Kif26b promotes the directional cell polarization and growth of HUVECs.
source: Interestingly, this study demonstrated that Kif26b promotes the directional cell polarization and growth of HUVECs (Guillabert-Gourgues et al., 2016), consistent with our finding that Kif26b controls the migration of cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge from a recent study, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling regulates Kif26b degradation, thereby influencing dynamic cellular processes such as the migratory behavior of cells.
source: Our study demonstrates that Wnt5a-Ror signaling regulates Kif26b degradation, thereby influencing dynamic cellular processes such as the migratory behavior of cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data in the study.

claim: By perturbing Kif26b function during embryogenesis, the study provides in vivo evidence that Kif26b mediates certain biological effects of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway in body axis elongation and PGC development.
source: Moreover, by perturbing Kif26b function during embryogenesis, we provide in vivo evidence that Kif26b mediates certain biological effects of the Wnt5a-Ror pathway in body axis elongation and PGC development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the zebrafish and mouse in vivo data.

claim: A Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b pathway comprises a conserved signaling cassette crucial for the execution of noncanonical Wnt functions.
source: Together, these findings suggest that a Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b pathway comprises a conserved signaling cassette crucial for the execution of noncanonical Wnt functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data in the study.

claim: Wnt5a-Ror signaling triggers the ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation of Kif26b.
source: Our observation that Wnt5a-Ror signaling triggers the ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation of Kif26b demonstrates that UPS-mediated proteolysis is a conserved strategy employed by both the canonical Wnt/β-catenin and the noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror pathways to control the cellular abundance of their respective downstream effectors (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data with proteasome and ubiquitin inhibitors, and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: UPS-mediated proteolysis is a conserved strategy employed by both the canonical Wnt/β-catenin and the noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror pathways to control the cellular abundance of their respective downstream effectors.
source: Our observation that Wnt5a-Ror signaling triggers the ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation of Kif26b demonstrates that UPS-mediated proteolysis is a conserved strategy employed by both the canonical Wnt/β-catenin and the noncanonical Wnt5a-Ror pathways to control the cellular abundance of their respective downstream effectors (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the mechanisms of canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling.

claim: Fzd and Dvl proteins are shared functional components of both canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling branches.
source: In addition, we provide further evidence that Fzd and Dvl proteins are shared functional components of both Wnt signaling branches.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing Fzd and Dvl involvement in Wnt5a-Ror-Kif26b signaling.

claim: The Wnt-Fzd-Dvl signaling module is an ancient and conserved feature common to multiple Wnt signaling systems.
source: Collectively, these observations suggest that the Wnt-Fzd-Dvl signaling module is an ancient and conserved feature common to multiple Wnt signaling systems.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the shared components of different Wnt signaling pathways.

claim: During evolution of the Wnt pathway, different signaling branches appear to have adopted additional regulatory mechanisms to achieve signaling and functional specificity.
source: During evolution of the pathway, different signaling branches appear to have adopted additional regulatory mechanisms to achieve signaling and functional specificity.
evidence: This is speculation about the evolution of Wnt signaling pathways.

claim: The canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway uses the Lrp5/6 receptors in conjunction with Fzd receptors to transmit a canonical Wnt signal across the plasma membrane.
source: For example, while the Wnt/β-catenin pathway uses the Lrp5/6 receptors in conjunction with Fzd receptors to transmit a canonical Wnt signal across the plasma membrane, the Wnt5a-Ror pathway uses Ror1/2 receptors, likely also in conjunction with Fzds, to transmit a noncanonical Wnt signal.
